newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish minister denies Aer Lingus for sale.
newsitem.headline: Irish minister denies Aer Lingus for sale.

text.p: Irish Transport Minister Alan Dukes said on Thursday that opposition charges that he planned to sell state carrier Aer Lingus were "stupid and unfounded".

Dukes said in a statement that he wanted Aer Lingus to explore the possibilities of entering into a strategic alliance "with or without the transfer of equity in order to ensure the continued success of the airline".

He was responding to comments by spokesmen for the opposition Fianna Fail party that the government was preparing to dispose of the airline after it posted a 130 percent rise in 1996 pretax profits to 40.9 million Irish pounds on Wednesday.
The airline has been mandated by its major shareholder, the Irish government, to consider an alliance in a market where consolidation and globalisation have become major trends.
The airline is due to report back to the government by the end of this year on possible alliances.

"I have taken this step because it seems to me to be a proper and prudent one in the context of today's firecely competitive air transport market and in the light of the generally-held views of how the market is likely to evolve in the years ahead," Dukes said.
